prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1173; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss came in reporting a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection. The driver involved is named on the policy, and the vehicle was towed to a repair facility for inspection.

Entry 2: Claimant's counsel confirmed representation and asked that all contact go through their office. Scene photos were uploaded, and they confirm some of the details the parties have described.

Entry 3: The vehicle inspection is complete. The damage to the rear bumper and trunk area is mostly in line with the described impact, and nothing found so far suggests earlier damage. The repair estimate is under review.

Entry 4: Initial medical records describe a neck strain, and the kind and force of the crash fit that injury well. No prior treatment to the same body area appears in the records received so far.

Entry 5: Recorded statement taken from the claimant through counsel. The account matched the first notice and every earlier conversation. It is still unclear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting at impact, so a follow-up question was sent.

Entry 6: No independent witnesses have come forward, so the file rests on the parties' accounts and the photos. Treatment has run somewhat longer than usual for this injury, and complete treatment records for the full period have been requested.

Entry 7: Coverage was confirmed in force at the time of loss, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy start. The claim stays open pending the outstanding treatment records and the response to the follow-up question.
